paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Conrad Blackburn Candidate's Full Name Conrad Blackburn Candidate's Pronouns he/him Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQ community? If so, please specify as you are comfortable* No, but I am a proud ally Office New York State Assembly District Number 70 Full Name of Campaign Committee(s) Friends of Conrad Blackburn Campaign Website conradforharlem.com Campaign Social Media Handles Twitter: @conradforharlem TikTok: @conradforharlem Instagram: @conradforharlem Facebook: facebook.com/conradforharlem If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. Yes What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? I’m a public defender and organizer committed to building power in working-class communities. I grew up poor, raised by a single mother, and have lived the struggles many in Harlem face. I defend New Yorkers in court while advancing policy, building coalitions, and passing laws. I’ve organized unions and navigated Albany’s politics. My work is rooted in lived experience, not polling—I fight to create a more just future for my community. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 1

[PDF page 2] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires I have had the opportunity to speak at multiple Trans Rights rallies, including those put on by Black Trans Mutual Aid and the New York City Democratic Socialists of America. When I speak at these rallies, I center the experiences of Black and Brown Trans Women who face an intersection of oppression. I also uplift Harlem’s history of being the center of New York City’s underground ball community, which many of Harlem’s politicians conveniently leave out. I also have called on NYU, and now Mount Sinai, to resume gender affirming care for those under 18. My campaign is dedicated to centering Trans voices and stories in everything we do. Additionally, as a child, to better afford the cost of living, my single mother moved our family in with two of her closest friends. These two queer women, who are like family to me, shaped me into the person I am today. They taught me how to show up for my community and the LGBTQ community. I thank these two powerful women for shaping me into a lifelong ally and advocate for the LGBTQ community. What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? First, one of my main priorities would be the Invest in Our New York legislative package. That includes S1622/A1281 (progressive income taxes), S953/A1971 (raising corporate taxes), S1439/A676 (capital gains tax), and S914/A2049 (heirs’ tax). These are incredibly important to making sure that New York can fund the many projects it needs to fund, whether that be universal childcare, expanding housing voucher access, funding healthcare, or more. The stakes for passing these tax the rich bills are only increased given the hostility of the Trump Administration, which has regularly attempted to pull funding from New York and other Blue states to coerce them to do the Trump Administration’s bidding. At a time when the federal government is cutting vital social services that Harlemites rely on like Medicare and SNAP, we must fill these spending gaps with guaranteed access to gender affirming care and LGBTQ New Yorkers’ access to PrEP. We will be able to fill this care gap and expand other critical social services for the LGBTQ community if we tax the rich. Second, believe that we should put immense focus into enacting the Social Housing Development Authority. The housing crisis is one of the most pressing crises affecting New Yorkers. Rents are too high, housing availability is at an all time low, and even New Yorkers with housing are crammed into smaller and smaller apartments. We cannot leave everything to private developers who, at the end of the day, care only about their bottom line. Having the government step in to build social housing, particularly social housing that is green and union built, will drastically help us tackle the housing crisis. We’ve seen how social housing has begun to help places like Montgomery County here in the States. And Vienna, the poster child for social housing, has been incredibly successful in ensuring that its residents have access to quality housing regardless of income. We can, should, and must bring that kind of housing here to New York. How can we say housing is a human right when we won’t even work to provide sufficient housing to every New Yorker. With truly affordable housing, we will be able to ensure that our LGBTQ neighbors do not have to choose between affording housing and healthcare or are not priced out of a safe state for them to live in. Third, I would work to pass a package of bills specifically targeted towards divesting from ICE and federal overreach via immigration enforcement. That means enacting New York for All, and not just a ban on 287(g) agreements as Governor Hochul has put forward. It also means enacting the Dignity, Not Detention Act to prevent using local facilities to house people detained for immigration purposes. And it means creating statewide access to representation for people with Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 2

[PDF page 3] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires immigration court cases. These are all obvious things that the State can do to massively slow down the deportation machine. And we must enact them now particularly as the Trump Administration attempts to use ICE as enforcers to make their targets swallow the administration’s agenda and ensure they are not allowed to enter NY hospitals. Many LGBTQ immigrants do not feel safe returning to their home countries. By ending any collusion with ICE and federal immigration enforcement, we can keep these members of the community safe in the country they have chosen to call their home. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. I am endorsed by New York City Democratic Socialists of America, United Auto Workers Region 9A, New York Working Families Party, New York Communities for Change, Citizen Action New York, New York Progressive Action Network, Met Council Action, Churches United for Fair Housing, TREEAge, and Run for Something. I am also endorsed by State Senators Jabari Brisport and Julia Salazar, State Assembly Members Claire Valdez, Diana Moreno, Emily Gallagher, and Sarahana Shresta, and City Council Members Alexa Avilés, Tiffany Caban, Shahana Hanif, and Chi Ossé. I am very proud to have the endorsement of Jaime Berman, the first trans person to hold elected office in Manhattan history. Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ candidates? Which ones? As this is my first time running for office, I have not been asked to endorse any candidates yet. Would you in the future endorse, appoint or financially support any candidate for public office, elected official, or political appointee with a record of opposing LGBTQ equality? If yes, please explain. * No! Our LGBTQ siblings are some of our nation’s most vulnerable people at this time, and to not support them is a moral failure. Across the nation, and in New York State, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ legislation, including restricting the rights of trans youth, bans on LGBTQ books in schools, limits on drag queen performances, and limits on gender affirming care for minors and adults. How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for the protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state, and country? I will use my voice as a legislator to call out anti-LGBTQ legislation. I will organize my colleagues in the Democratic Caucus to oppose any attacks on the LGBTQ community and educate those who are on the fence about why we must stand together to protect this community. I will introduce and support legislation to further protect the community, including allowing all New Yorkers to play sports with their identified gender. I will use my platform to educate constituents and New Yorkers about LGBTQ history and issues and host events with drag queens, LGBTQ organizers, and elders in the community. For Trans Day of Visibility, I highlighted my district's long history with the Trans community. Throughout the rest of my campaign and my tenure in office I will continue to center stories of LGBTQ people in Harlem and around New York State. The LGBTQ community has historically been overpoliced, and research shows that law enforcement continues to disproportionately target marginalized people: What do you view as the New York State Legislature's role in Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 3

[PDF page 4] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires ensuring law enforcement oversight, funding, and role in meeting the needs of marginalized communities? What, if any, relevant policy proposals do you support regarding law enforcement? As a public defender, I have seen both how over policing targets marginalized people unfairly and how the State Legislature can enact policies to solve this issue. We need to respond to mental health crises with mental health professionals, and I would work to advance legislation to fund mental health professionals as first responders. I strongly support Daniel’s Law (S3670/A4617) to ensure that we’re using public health responses to address mental health issues rather than public safety ones. Anything that decreases the number of interactions between law enforcement and any marginalized group will result in better outcomes for marginalized people. I also believe that we should do a better job of preventing law enforcement officers from hopping from place to place after being charged with serious misconduct. Officers upon being fired in one jurisdiction may simply travel to another jurisdiction to take a new position as an officer and begin acting in the same manner that originally resulted in their firing. By banning the appointment of such officers (S8514/A5132), we can make sure that no one is functionally above the law simply because they have decided to move or resign when charged. And a very simple bill we should pass is New York for All (S2235/A3506). This creates a prohibition on law enforcement on sharing information with ICE and Customs and Border Patrol and regulates what questions state and local law enforcement can ask about someone’s immigration status. This will specifically protect our immigrant neighbors. One final piece of legislation I want to suggest here is the Family Miranda Act (S551/A1234). Systemically, child protective services end up targeting poorer communities of color. And LGBTQ+ people of color are substantially more likely than others to be subjected to separation from their children. Requiring that agents of the family regulatory system provide information about the rights of caregivers at the onset of any interaction is important to curbing those structural issues of racism and anti-queer bias. It also will provide opportunities to challenge adverse decisions against caregivers based on violations of these rights, giving us a way of holding family regulation law enforcement members accountable. Transitioning from some legislative solutions to thinking about the budget, the easiest thing to advocate for is a focus on increasing funding for projects and initiatives that support our communities rather than constantly increasing law enforcement funding. For example, increasing funding for healthcare or transportation will actively do more to keep marginalized New Yorkers safer and healthier than law enforcement funding. We can focus on funding transit projects that help transit deserts become transit rich, which is important as transit deserts so often fall upon people of color. Likewise, funding healthcare ensures that New Yorkers are able to keep their healthcare while funding different forms of medical care. This means providing funding for clinics that may traditionally scrape by financially, but also are the ones that provide gender-affirming care. I also believe that the legislature has a very direct role in oversight. Committees can hold hearings on certain topics, inviting government officials, advocates, and the public to testify on the record about issues. As a member of the Assembly, I would advocate to hold oversight hearings on law enforcement responses to crime to get police and district attorneys on the record about their policing and charging decisions, and to provide the public with the opportunity to discuss ideas openly and before the legislature on how to reign in law enforcement abuses that are so often visited on Black folks, trans folks, immigrants, and other marginalized groups. A hearing, additionally, puts more of the legislature’s weight behind addressing a topic as opposed to having one elected official propose a solution and try to get it done from scratch. Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 4

[PDF page 5] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Similarly, holding hearings would allow us to examine what kind of surveillance technology law enforcement is procuring and how that technology is being used. Oftentimes such technology may be used, that is, at best, in Fourth Amendment gray area. Using high tech surveillance so often puts marginalized communities under scrutiny other communities do not face. And it can be used to retributively charge and prosecute people for exercising their rights, as we saw happen to some during anti-genocide protests. Being able to examine what tech is procured, how it is used, and what policies govern its use in a public forum will allow us to perform meaningful oversight on law enforcement and prevent violation of people's constitutional rights. And it will allow us to formulate legislative responses that address specific problems and reign in abuse of power. This is all the more important as law enforcement begins to rely on AI, particularly in the facial recognition context. AI is trained on biased data that tends to correlate criminality with race. This increases the chance of false positives that may lead to Black and Brown New Yorkers being subjected to increased criminal legal contact. We must limit AI use in law enforcement contexts because it truly hurts our communities. New York State is experiencing a housing crisis, and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do you intend to ensure that any housing plan is equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? I believe that to best help New Yorkers experiencing homelessness we need to build a robust social service program and work towards moving these individuals to independent housing where they are supported with job placement, any medical help they may require, and are given a way to build community. We need to decriminalize homelessness in the subways and other public areas by repealing fines and fees that often disproportionally hurt Black and Brown New Yorkers. We must also ensure that the State fully funds the Housing Access Voucher program to help people experiencing homelessness access housing. We also know that many trans and queer New Yorkers do not feel safe entering the current shelter system. We must pass legislation to ensure that trans New Yorkers are able to access the shelters that accurately reflect their gender identity. I will increase funding for trans specific shelters and work to create programs to educate shelter staff about trans identities to better serve these constituents. Our current affordable housing plans often leave out marginalized groups because they price out our most vulnerable. In order to expand low and moderate income housing, I would support funding and building a state construction authority that specializes in building housing and transit infrastructure across the state as called for in the Social Housing Development Act carried by Assemblymember Emily Gallagher and Senator Cordell Cleare. Currently, there is a vacuum in terms of building expertise because the United States government does not do any building directly, but instead all construction work is paid out to the highest bidder. This means, we don't have a program to ensure the building of desperately needed housing, transit, or public infrastructure is built effectively to minimize costs. This would also create more union jobs across New York. And building social housing greatly benefits low and moderate income people. We’ve seen the success it has had in places like Vienna, Austria or Montgomery County, Maryland. In today’s political climate, what role should the New York Legislature play in protecting and expanding access to comprehensive reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare? Will you commit to defending access to abortion care and gender-affirming care for both adults and youth, including taking legislative action to prevent hospitals Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 5

[PDF page 6] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires and healthcare systems—such as NYU Langone Health—from restricting or ending lifesaving care due to political pressure or federal intimidation? * We are currently seeing large healthcare centers, like NYU Langone and Mount Sinai, who share many donors with the current president, cave to illegal executive orders and deny life saving healthcare from trans youth. It is very likely that these hospitals could continue to cut care and not provide abortion care or gender affirming care to adults. I will do everything in my power to combat this. Denying abortion or gender affirming care is illegal in New York State after we enshrined these in our state constitution in 2024. To ensure that this care continues, I would work with Attorney General James’ office and use every possible angle to hold these hospitals accountable, including denying funding at the state level and exploring removing charitable status for non compliance with New York State law. At the same time, I will push to provide funding to local clinics that are bravely continuing this care to make sure that all New Yorkers are able to continue accessing this care. I would also work to expand access to this care at public health centers, like New York City’s Health and Hospitals, by increasing their budget and earmarking funds for gender affirming care and abortion care. Privacy Amendment S8603 (Ramos) / A9377 (Shimsky) This amendment would enshrine a fundamental right to privacy in the New York Constitution, protecting personal decisions, bodily autonomy, and limiting government surveillance beyond federal standards. It is especially critical for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers whose sensitive data could otherwise be misused or weaponized. Yes Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE) S6901A (Salazar) / A7496 (Gonzalez-Rojas) This bill ensures age-appropriate, inclusive sex education statewide that reflects national standards. It reduces stigma, affirms LGBTQ+ students, and promotes safer, more informed school environments. Yes New York for All Act S2235 (Gounardes) / A3506 (Reyes) This bill limits state and local involvement in immigration enforcement, protecting immigrant families and public safety. It is vital for safeguarding LGBTQ+ immigrants who face heightened risks of targeting and discrimination. Yes Holding Police Accountable by Strengthening the Civilian Complaint Review Board S4354 (Bailey) / A126 (Cruz) This act expands the CCRB’s authority to investigate bias-based policing, which disproportionately harms LGBTQ+ people, particularly LGBTQ+ New Yorkers of color. It is a necessary step toward real accountability and trust in law enforcement. Yes The Gender Identity Respect Dignity and Safety Act (GIRDS) (A5478A - Gallagher/ S1049A Salazar) This bill ensures incarcerated transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals are treated with dignity, respected in placement, and provided gender-affirming necessities. It significantly improves safety and reduces abuse in correctional settings. Yes Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 6
